requirements.title: A control information list governs data transfer
requirements.definition: A control information list is an io-control-spec-list and governs data transfer.

pending.control-list-governs-data-transfer: Future paired READ/WRITE controls vary exactly one io-control-spec, such as FMT= versus NML= or POS= versus sequential positioning, after establishing distinct nonblank/nonzero records; assert only the portable data-transfer effect owned by the varied specifier and not processor-dependent unit numbers or status text.

requirements.oracle: Plans are pending and source-derived. Negative plans change one source property from the conforming control and do not require a particular diagnostic message, severity, exit status, or printed rule number.

requirements.title: io-control-spec syntax enumerates unit, format, namelist, control, branch, status, position, record, and size specifiers
requirements.definition: An io-control-spec is one of the listed forms: optionally keyworded UNIT= io-unit, FMT= format, NML= namelist-group-name, ADVANCE=, ASYNCHRONOUS=, BLANK=, DECIMAL=, DELIM=, END=, EOR=, ERR=, ID=, IOMSG=, IOSTAT=, LEADING_ZERO=, PAD=, POS=, REC=, ROUND=, SIGN=, or SIZE= with the indicated expression, variable, label, or name operand. The bracketed UNIT=, FMT=, and NML= alternatives are the syntax source for omitted-keyword admission; C1211, C1218, and C1219 supply the placement restrictions.

pending.unit-specifier-form: Compile conforming controls with `READ(UNIT=unit,FMT='(I1)') value` and `READ(unit,'(I1)') value`; the omitted UNIT= admission is owned by R1213 and the positional placement remains constrained by C1211. The paired syntax negative deletes the io-unit operand or keyword punctuation only.
pending.format-specifier-form: Compile conforming controls with `FMT='(I1)'` and an unkeyworded second-item format; omitted FMT= admission is owned by R1213 and second-item placement remains constrained by C1218. The paired syntax negative deletes the format operand or keyword punctuation only.
pending.namelist-specifier-form: Compile conforming controls with `NML=group` and an unkeyworded second-item namelist group after declaring `namelist /group/ value`; omitted NML= admission is owned by R1213 and placement remains constrained by C1219. The paired syntax negative deletes the group operand or keyword punctuation only.
pending.advance-specifier-form: Compile a conforming single-image data-transfer statement containing ADVANCE='NO' or 'YES' in an otherwise minimal control list that also satisfies the applicable C1210-C1231 constraints; the paired syntax negative deletes the required operand or keyword punctuation for this alternative only, so parsing reaches R1213.
pending.asynchronous-specifier-form: Compile a conforming single-image data-transfer statement containing ASYNCHRONOUS='YES' or 'NO' in an otherwise minimal control list that also satisfies the applicable C1210-C1231 constraints; the paired syntax negative deletes the required operand or keyword punctuation for this alternative only, so parsing reaches R1213.

requirements.title: An io-control-spec-list contains an io-unit and positional io-units are first
requirements.definition: An io-unit shall be specified in an io-control-spec-list; if UNIT= is omitted, the io-unit shall be the first item in the list. The permission to omit UNIT= is the bracketed [UNIT=] syntax in R1213; C1211 records the presence obligation and the first-item restriction for that admitted form.

requirements.title: ERR, EOR, and END labels are same-scope branch target statements
requirements.definition: For each ERR=, EOR=, or END= specifier, the label shall identify a branch target statement, and that branch target statement shall appear in the same inclusive scope as the data transfer statement.

pending.err-label-branch-target: Diagnostic/control pair changes only the ERR= label target from a same-scope CONTINUE branch target to a same-scope FORMAT statement label, keeping the label defined but not a branch target.
pending.err-label-same-inclusive-scope: Diagnostic/control pair changes only the placement of label 100: the control has `100 CONTINUE` in the same inclusive scope as `READ(...,ERR=100)`, while the invalid source places `100 CONTINUE` as a branch target statement in a different inclusive scope (for example an internal procedure) and has no same-scope label 100. Future fixture review must retain the branch-target property and attribute the required diagnostic to C1215's same-inclusive-scope obligation, not to ERR= semantics or IOMSG text.
pending.eor-label-branch-target: Diagnostic/control pair uses a nonadvancing formatted READ with ADVANCE='NO' and changes only the EOR= label target from CONTINUE to FORMAT.
pending.eor-label-same-inclusive-scope: Diagnostic/control pair uses a nonadvancing formatted READ with `ADVANCE='NO',EOR=100`; the control's `100 CONTINUE` branch target is in the same inclusive scope, while the invalid source moves that branch target statement to a different inclusive scope and changes no EOR or ADVANCE spelling.
pending.end-label-branch-target: Diagnostic/control pair changes only the END= label target from a same-scope CONTINUE branch target to a same-scope FORMAT statement label.
pending.end-label-same-inclusive-scope: Diagnostic/control pair changes only the placement of label 100 for `END=100`: the control labels a same-inclusive-scope CONTINUE branch target, while the invalid source places the branch target statement in a different inclusive scope with no same-scope label 100.

requirements.oracle: C1215 has two independent obligations for each ERR=, EOR=, and END= label: branch-target statement identity and same-inclusive-scope placement. The branch-target negatives keep the label in scope but change only the statement kind; the same-scope negatives keep a branch target statement with the label but move it outside the data transfer statement's inclusive scope. Future fixtures must compile a conforming same-scope control and must not rely on IOMSG text, branch execution, or a particular diagnostic wording.

The permission to omit FMT= is the bracketed [FMT=] syntax in R1213; C1218 supplies only the placement restrictions for that admitted positional format.

pending.eor-requires-advance: No pure C1224-only invalid program exists because omitting ADVANCE= when EOR= appears also violates p2's stricter unnumbered requirement that ADVANCE= with value NO appear. The future diagnostic/control pair may remove only `ADVANCE='NO'` from a conforming nonadvancing formatted external READ with `EOR=100` and a same-scope branch target; that invalid source violates C1224 and p2, but C1224 is the only numbered rule in the overlap and therefore the only rule with a required diagnostic. The fixture must not claim isolated p2 coverage or assert diagnostic wording.

requirements.oracle: C1224 requires presence of ADVANCE= whenever EOR= appears. requirements.oracle: C1230 is split: S12.6.2.1-006 records the list-directed and namelist admissions for DELIM=, while C1230 records the required diagnostic when DELIM= is used with an explicit nonasterisk format and no namelist group.

requirements.title: ID variables have at least default-integer decimal exponent range
requirements.definition: The scalar-int-variable in an id-variable shall have a decimal exponent range no smaller than that of default integer.

pending.default-integer-id-range-control: Positive control declares the ID variable as default integer, initializes it to a nonzero sentinel, and uses it only with a conforming `ASYNCHRONOUS='YES'` file-unit-number transfer.
pending.narrow-id-range-no-portable-negative: No portable isolated negative is registered: the standard does not require a processor to provide an integer kind with decimal exponent range smaller than default integer, and kind selector values are processor dependent. Future processor-profile tests may add such a diagnostic only after proving the smaller range independently.

requirements.title: EOR also requires ADVANCE=NO
requirements.definition: If an EOR= specifier appears, an ADVANCE= specifier with value NO shall also appear.

pending.eor-advance-no-required: Source-control plan pairs a conforming nonadvancing formatted external READ with `ADVANCE='NO', EOR=100` against a program changing only the ADVANCE value to 'YES'; C1224 remains satisfied, so this unnumbered p2 obligation is isolated without claiming a required numbered diagnostic.

requirements.title: Format or namelist controls make a data transfer formatted; absence makes it unformatted
requirements.definition: If the data transfer statement contains a format or namelist-group-name, the statement is a formatted input/output statement; otherwise, it is an unformatted input/output statement.

pending.format-control-makes-formatted: Future control writes integer 7 to a character buffer initialized to sentinels using explicit format '(I1)' and expects exact '7', proving formatted transfer without relying on external representation.
pending.namelist-control-makes-formatted: Future namelist control initializes all group objects to nondefault values and performs namelist I/O, but leaves exact namelist spelling to 13.11; this facet records the formatted classification only.
pending.absence-makes-unformatted: Future external unformatted WRITE/READ round trip uses a file-unit-number and nondefault integer sentinel values; it asserts only successful recovery of the written value, not file bytes.

requirements.title: Control-character specifier values use limited lists, ignore trailing blanks, and ignore case
requirements.definition: The ADVANCE=, ASYNCHRONOUS=, DECIMAL=, BLANK=, DELIM=, LEADING_ZERO=, PAD=, SIGN=, and ROUND= specifiers have limited lists of character values; trailing blanks are ignored and values are interpreted without regard to case.

pending.limited-character-value-lists: Future diagnostics use one specifier-specific invalid value after the relevant later subclause supplies the complete permitted list; this p4 facet does not invent a list beyond the pinned source.
pending.trailing-blanks-ignored: Future positive pair uses a value such as `ADVANCE='NO   '` or `ASYNCHRONOUS='YES   '` in a context that otherwise satisfies C1223/C1226, and compares only the same portable transfer/status property as the no-blank control.
pending.case-insensitive-values: Future positive pair changes only the case of a permitted value such as `ADVANCE='no'` versus `ADVANCE='NO'`, with all data targets initialized to nondefault sentinels before the transfer.

Mixed-form decision: ASYNCHRONOUS= syntax is admitted by R1213 and value YES by C1225; C1226 is retained as the file-unit-number restriction for YES.
Mixed admission/restriction split: C1230 admits DELIM= for list-directed or namelist formatting and restricts explicit nonasterisk-format use without namelist.
Permission/admission half for DELIM= with asterisk format or namelist-group-name.

review_rationale: Source registration for 12.6.2/12.6.2.1, the io-control-spec list (batch153). Every unit hash-verified against the pinned census by an independent reviewer across two rounds. Numbered rules R1213, R1214 and C1210-C1231 are registered with diagnostic facets only where the constraint alone is violated by a one-property change. Round 1 found missed permission/restriction splits (C1223's 'only in', C1230's either-or), a compound obligation lost from C1215 (branch target AND same inclusive scope), and a C1224 negative that also violates unnumbered p2; all resolved, with C1224 recorded as the only diagnosable rule in that unavoidable overlap. Source accounting only.
